findings.claim: The new guard `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` around `kill()` is always False for spawn-context processes. On a hang restart the old flusher is never killed. A replacement starts on the same shards, the orphan is no longer monitored because `process_healthy_since[process_index]` is overwritten, and both processes can flush the same segments. Up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS orphans can build up per index. The base called `kill()` unconditionally.
findings.evidence: `mp.get_context('spawn').Process` builds `SpawnProcess`, whose MRO is (SpawnProcess, BaseProcess, object). `python3 -I -c "import multiprocessing as m; p=m.get_context('spawn').Process(target=print); assert isinstance(p, m.Process)"` raises AssertionError. mattpocock, open-code-review and superpowers ran this check locally; ponytail cites the same check.
findings.reason: Severities were Important x3 and Critical x1. Normalised to Critical because this silently disables the existing hang-recovery kill in production, and a hang can be one slow loop. A red check exists for the type test. A flusher-level red test still has to drive `_ensure_processes_alive`, and no seat wrote one.

findings.claim: In `join`, `terminate()` sits behind the same `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check. It is therefore a no-op for SpawnProcess, so flushers are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance. The bug predates the patch, and the patch copies it into the new per-process loop.
findings.evidence: Same MRO and the same failing one-liner as the kill-guard finding. All seats note that the check existed on base and is repeated in the patched loop.
findings.reason: This code is in the patched loop, and fixing it is a prerequisite for the join-break finding to matter. It predates the patch, so record it as pre-existing. It can be made red with the same isinstance check.

findings.claim: In `join`, once the deadline passes, `break` leaves the loop before `terminate()` runs for the current process and every later one. The base always reached its terminate step.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the code at 336-347. The bug is masked today because terminate is already a no-op through the isinstance bug, and it becomes live once that is fixed. open-code-review assumes arroyo calls join with a finite timeout on revocation and did not confirm this.
findings.reason: Rated Important by open-code-review and Minor by superpowers. Normalised to Important because the companion fix to line 346 makes it live. Unverified: it is reasoned only, with no red test yet.

findings.claim: Each process gets its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`, so `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` becomes a per-process limit. With P processes the consumer flushes up to P times the documented per-cycle maximum, and the `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure threshold rises the same way, so backpressure starts later.
findings.evidence: `buffer.py:382-383` computes `ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards))` over only the process's subset. The option is documented at `options/defaults.py:2716` as a per-cycle maximum. This does not apply at the CLI default of 1, but it does with `max_processes=None` or N > 1.
findings.reason: Reasoned by all seats, and mattpocock lists it as outside its seat and unchecked. Needs a red test with more than one process before fixing. Unverified.

findings.claim: Each `submit()` calls `get_memory_info()` once per per-process buffer. Every buffer talks to the same cluster, so that is N INFO sweeps that add up duplicate nodes. The ratio is unchanged, so this is redundant I/O on the consumer's main thread.
findings.evidence: All buffers use `get_redis_client()` → `SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER` (`buffer.py:117`), and `get_memory_info` is `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`. Reasoned from the code.
findings.reason: Accepted Minor. Fix by calling a single buffer once, as on base.

findings.claim: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code with no callers. Restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards`.
findings.evidence: Grep across src/ and tests/ finds only the definition.

findings.claim: The `shard` tag value is a comma-joined list of all the process's partitions, not one shard. It changes on every rebalance, and at the default of one process it holds the whole partition list, which gives high tag cardinality.
findings.evidence: `shard_tag` joins the process's shard ids at L185 and L195.
findings.reason: Accepted Minor.

findings.evidence: CLI default at `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:433`.
findings.reason: Accepted Minor. Correct the docstring.

findings.claim: The defaults disagree: `max_processes=None` on SpanFlusher and the factory means one process per shard, while the CLI default of 1 means a single process. As a result, test_basic and test_backpressure exercise the per-shard path and not the production configuration.

findings.claim: `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no lower bound. A negative value empties `process_to_shards_map` and raises KeyError on `i % -1`, and 0 silently means one process per shard.
